title: Alvaro de Sande, fragment partly in cipher, deciphered between the lines
shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera S, Sande (de), Alvaro, c. 59
folio_note: c. 59r: about 24 lines carry cipher mixed with Spanish clear text, roughly 1,000 signs (not a short fragment). c. 59v not examined.
status: Record: 'In spagnolo. Frammento di documento parzialmente cifrato, decifrato nell'interlinea.' The other ~30 Sande records do not mention cipher. Manifest uuid(s): c8490bb4-f0bf-41a3-bd85-4c41aead033f. Looked at by WAINUT on 3 Nov 2026, not started beyond the images: a letter cipher of signs like Greek capitals (B, T, Y, Omega, Lambda, Sigma, Psi and others) with one letter written above each sign, so the pairs are letter to letter. Content: a military report; clear names seen on the overview only (Lanzave, Ferrando de Fernando, the maestre de campo, Juan Bautista), unverified. A transcription job, not a break.
why: A small Spanish military cipher sample with its clear.
verify: Sign inventory, two sign-first passes, gloss transcription, key from the pairs, frozen held-out test. Compare 'Una cifra imperial en Roma (1543)', Estudios Románicos (Murcia).
score_note: Scored from the Lodovico record and a low-resolution look at the scans during the Nov 2026 Estense sweep (research/wainut_leads_2026-11-03/)

title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski → Pál Ráday: draft letters on Prussian mediation in the Rákóczi war, partly in cipher, with the key sent in June 1704
correspondents: Daniel Ernst Jablonski (Prussian court preacher, Berlin) → Pál Ráday (Rákóczi's envoy, later chancellor)
shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Nachl. August Hermann Francke, 11,2/14 : 62 (24 Jun 1704, sends the key), 11,2/14 : 71 (4 Oct 1704, key not received, new key promised), 11,2/14 : 75 (8 Nov 1704, partly in cipher, decoded in some places); Briefkonzeptbuch Jablonski 1701-1704
folio_note: three drafts in Jablonski's letter-draft book; amount of cipher not known; no. 75 is the one with cipher passages left only partly decoded
status: Kalliope DE-611-HS-2910511, -2910521, -2910525 (subject 'Geheimschrift'). No. 62: 'übermittelt er den Schlüssel für eine Geheimschrift'; no. 71: recipients never got the key, copy with a new key sent via Vienna; no. 75: 'Teilweise in Geheimschrift verfaßter Text, der an einigen Stellen dekodiert ist' (partial decode). Not on DECODE (no Berlin/Wolfenbüttel holder in the repo's DECODE dumps). Not in catalogue or leads; the repo's Rákóczi targets (R483 reading) name 'domino Jablonski', so this is the Berlin end of a channel already touched.
why: Prussia's secret mediation between Rákóczi's Hungarians and Vienna in 1704, from the Berlin side, and a key that may read Ráday's received originals in Budapest.
score_note: Scored from the Kalliope descriptions during the Nov 2026 HAB/SBB sweep (research/wainut_leads_2026-11-03/); not viewed
verify: Find scans: the PRINT Migration Network (stars.library.ucf.edu, collection printmigrationnetwork-franckenachlass) hosts PDFs of single letters from these draft books; ask SBB for the 11,2/14 volume otherwise. Check Benda (ed.), Ráday Pál iratai I, 1703-1706 (Budapest 1955) for the received copies.
prior_art: unclear (checked 3 Nov 2026: repo grep, DECODE dumps, web search): Ráday's papers are edited (Benda, Ráday Pál iratai, 1955/1961), which may print the received letters in clear; drafts not checked
access_note: no SBB digitisation link in Kalliope; single letters of the Jablonski draft books are online as PDFs in the PRINT Migration Network (UCF STARS), not yet matched to these numbers

shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Nachl. August Hermann Francke, 11,2/15 : 8 (13 Mar 1705), 11,2/15 : 13 (18 Apr 1705), 11,2/15 : 33 (11 Sep 1705)
folio_note: nos. 8 and 13: cipher written above or parallel to the Latin text; no. 13 also discusses the encryption itself; no. 33 tagged 'Geheimschrift'
status: Kalliope DE-611-HS-2910535, -2910540, -2910560. Descriptions: 'Wortlaut teilweise mit einer Geheimschrift überschrieben'; 'teilweise parallel zum Text mit Geheimschrift geschriebenen Brief ... technische Details des Briefverkehrs, die unter anderem die Verschlüsselung betreffen'. These drafts carry the plaintext, so they are a key source rather than an open ciphertext. Not on DECODE; not in repo.
why: Plaintext-plus-cipher pairs that rebuild the Jablonski-Ráday key, which can then read cipher passages without plaintext (1704 no. 75, 1712 no. 91, and received copies in Hungary).
